newsitem.title: USA: Justice slowness may kill FBI hearings - Specter.
newsitem.headline: Justice slowness may kill FBI hearings - Specter.

text.p: Sen. Arlen Specter said Tuesday that if the Justice Department fails to finish a needed report in time for an upcoming hearing on FBI treatment of former Olympic pipe bomb suspect Richard Jewell, he may have to cancel the hearing.

The Pennsylvania Republican has invited Jewell and FBI Director Louis Freeh to testify before his Senate Judiciary subcommittee in a one-day hearing Dec. 10 about last summer's deadly bomb attack at the Olympics in Atlanta. Specter said he was waiting for a Justice Department report on the matter.
"I planned to have this hearing several weeks ago and I deferred it at Director Freeh's request until that report was finished," Specter said in an interview.
The government cleared Jewell Oct. 26 of any role in the bombing, which left two people dead and more than 100 injured at downtown Atlanta's Centennial Olympic Park.
Specter said his subcommittee wants to look into the FBI questioning of Jewell and news leaks that identified Jewell as a suspect, but he needs the Justice Department report.
"I'm not sure we are going to be able to go ahead," Specter said, adding he would raise the issue with Deputy Attorney General Jamie Gorelick at a meeting later in the day.
"I'll be talking to her about this," he said.

Justice Department spokesman Bert Brandenburg said the report would be completed as quickly as possible but added: "It is normal with investigations to not put an artificial deadline on because you don't want investigators to run risks or take shortcuts in arriving at the truth."
The Atlanta Journal-Constitution turned down an invitation to testify at the Jewell hearings, it reported Tuesday.
"Our stories about the bombing have conveyed all the information we have on this topic," the newspaper quoted editor Ron Martin as saying.
